The Korea Foundation grant’s purpose is “to establish an endowment for the creation and maintenance of a new permanent full-tenured professorship of Korean Studies at the University”. Conditions of the grant include: The Professorship shall be established within the Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures. The course assignments of the Professor shall be consistent with efforts to advance Korean studies and the guidelines of the Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures. The Professor shall assume a leading role in developing new academic courses and reinforcing the University’s existing Korean studies programs.
The University shall appoint the Professor from among those qualified candidates who satisfy the following requirements: the qualified candidate shall (i) focus on Korean Social Science and Policy as the primary subject of their research and teaching; (ii) focus on Korea in more than fifty percent (50%) of their research and teaching activities and conduct such research using primary sources published in the Korean language; (iii) publish the findings of such research in the English language and possibly in the Korean language.
The University shall provide the Foundation with a copy of the Professor’s curriculum vitae and a copy of the employment agreement executed between the Professor and the University as soon as the appointment procedures are completed
The restrictions in this contract relate to admission of students.  Students have to be admitted to the joint program.

The University shall appoint the Professor from among those qualified candidates to focus on Modern Korean History as the primary subject of his/her research and education, focus on Korea in more than fifty percent of his/her research and education activities and conduct such research using primary sources published in the Korean language, be proficient in the Korean language, and publish the findings of such research in the English language, and possibly in the Korean language.
The University shall ensure that the Professor teaches at least four Korean Studies courses each academic year. The University shall ensure that the Professor assumes a leadership role in the development of Korean Studies courses and course materials as well as the efforts to advance Korean Studies at the University. The Parties understand and agree that this position will be a tenured professor position or tenure-track assistant professor position and will be eligible for leave time pursuant to University policies and procedures. These standard University practices shall be allowed as part of the Professor’s appointment.
